assumptions: Because spec_json and upstream_lists are empty, the twelve state names were synthesized from the NL-described operating conditions and priority branches.
The model is a condition-classification abstraction: forced guard transitions reselect the active state from current PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity inputs rather than storing additional mode memory.
Pgmax is treated as a battery dispatch/charging margin capacity because the NL cites Pgmax/5 as a low-SoC charging margin but does not define a separate battery maximum power variable.
Pd2max was introduced as the DG2 capacity bound because the NL mentions DG1/DG2 and all thermal resources but only names Pd1max explicitly.
Load cut-in/cut-out is represented as aggregate load command flags because the NL does not provide individual load classes or load-shedding priority.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging or to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, the EMS serves all ship demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, residual renewable power is treated as spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows the priority: RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows the stated priority: RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable, LNG before diesel units.

scenario_results.description: default-init dispatch with PL=0 and no RES should select ZeroLoadNoRES and cut out loads/generators.
scenario_results.name: default_init_zero_load_no_res

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start wildcard classification: with PL=0, RES>0, and SoC below 0.95, RES should charge the battery.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_res_charges_battery_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start SoC boundary probe: with PL=0, RES>0, and SoC exactly 0.95, RES should be spare, not battery charge.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_res_spare_at_full_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start SoC below-boundary probe: when RES covers positive PL and SoC is below 0.95, residual RES should charge batteries.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_load_charges_battery_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start SoC boundary probe: when RES covers positive PL and SoC is exactly 0.95, residual RES should become spare power.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_load_spare_at_full_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start SoC suitability and capacity boundary probe: with SoC exactly 0.2 and deficit within Pgmax, batteries should cover the deficit before LNG.
scenario_results.name: battery_discharge_at_suitable_soc_and_pgmax_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start low-SoC probe: when deficit is LNG-coverable and SoC is below 0.2, LNG should cover load plus Pgmax/5 charging margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_cover_low_soc_adds_pgmax_charging_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start priority probe: with suitable SoC but deficit greater than Pgmax and within LNG capacity, LNG should cover before diesel units.
scenario_results.name: lng_cover_without_battery_when_deficit_exceeds_pgmax

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start diesel low-SoC probe: when LNG alone cannot cover and SoC is below 0.2, LNG+DG1 should cover load plus Pd1max/10 charging margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_low_soc_adds_pd1_charging_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start SoC suitability boundary probe: with SoC exactly 0.2 and deficit needing DG1 but not DG2, LNG+DG1 should serve the deficit without charging margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_at_suitable_soc_without_charging_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start last-priority probe: when deficit exceeds LNG+DG1 but is within LNG+DG1+DG2, all thermal units should cut in and no battery discharge is needed.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_dg2_last_priority_within_all_thermal_capacity

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start overload probe: when demand exceeds all RES and thermal resources, all thermal units should activate and remaining lack should be battery discharge in the illegal overload support state.
scenario_results.name: extreme_overload_uses_all_thermal_and_battery_support

evidence: NL: "The twelve finite states are selected by logical transition conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC."
DSL: 12 leaf states including ZeroLoadCharge, RESCoverCharge, BatteryDischarge, LNGCoverLowSoCCharge, LNGDG1DG2, and ExtremeOverloadBatterySupport.
DSL guards use PL, Ppv + Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, Pgmax, Pd1max, and Pd2max to select dispatch states.
sim_summary: ok=true, n_scenarios=16, n_scenarios_passed=16.
findings.summary: The DSL is broadly faithful to the NL operating logic: it models the twelve dispatch states, RES coverage behavior, zero-load charging/spare behavior, SoC thresholds, LNG-before-diesel priority, low-SoC charging margins, and the extreme overload diagnostic branch.

grounding_map.source_summary assumption: "The model is a condition-classification abstraction... rather than storing additional mode memory."
findings.summary: The model is a condition-classification abstraction with no temporal events or mode memory beyond the currently selected state. This is acceptable for the provided NL, which emphasizes logical state selection, but it does simplify time-varying operation into instantaneous reclassification.

evidence: NL: "The overload completion state is illegal... EMS activates all thermal generating units, covers the lack by battery discharge, and the state shall never occur in practice."
DSL guard: "PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw < PL && PL - Ppv - Pw > eng3_Pmax + Pd1max + Pd2max" selects ExtremeOverloadBatterySupport.
DSL ExtremeOverloadBatterySupport sets requested_generator_power = eng3_Pmax + Pd1max + Pd2max, battery_discharge_power = remaining deficit, all generator cut-ins = 1, and illegal_overload = 1.
findings.summary: The illegal overload branch is reachable, but it explicitly marks the violation with illegal_overload=1 and implements the NL-described all-thermal plus battery-support behavior. Under the review guidance, this is an admitted diagnostic/fail-safe abstraction rather than a blocking unsafe recovery.
